234: Sannae Myeongsu Tourist Farm is located in Gamsan-ri, Sannae-myeon, Gyeongju, Gyeongsangbuk-do. It is about 25 km from Gyeongju City Hall, reached by following Geonpo Saneop-ro and Danseok-ro by car. The journey takes around 30 minutes. Planted with a variety of trees, the campground offers an exceptionally natural setting. Around a pond are 24 standard camping pitches with decking or crushed-stone surfaces. Caravans and trailers are welcome at no additional charge. Visitors can try catching fish from spring through autumn and sledding in winter. Nearby Hwarang Hill and Gungmin Healing Park are easy to include in the same trip.
243: Tohamsan Rak Glamping is located on Bobul-ro in Gyeongju, Gyeongsangbuk-do. Around five minutes from Bulguksa Temple and the Bomun Tourist Complex, it overlooks the open expanse of Hadong Reservoir immediately below. Both vacation cottages and glamping accommodations are available, with an outdoor swimming pool, barbecue area, and basketball court. There is no shop at the glamping site. A medium-sized supermarket is a ten-minute drive away, so it is best to buy necessary supplies before arriving.

Gyeongju National Museum is one of Korea's leading museums, offering an overview of Silla's cultural heritage. It presents the condensed history of the thousand-year kingdom, which lasted from 57 BC to AD 935. Visiting the museum first to gain background knowledge before exploring Gyeongju's historic sites makes for a more rewarding trip. The museum comprises five permanent exhibition areas—the Silla History Gallery, Silla Art Gallery, Wolji Gallery, Silla Millennium Storage, and outdoor exhibition—as well as a special exhibition gallery. The Silla History Gallery traces Silla's history, while the Silla Art Gallery displays its magnificent artistic culture and artifacts.
The Wolji Gallery focuses on royal life and culture during the Unified Silla period. The outdoor exhibition displays around 1,300 stone artifacts, including Buddhist bells, stone pagodas, stone Buddhas, stone lanterns, and stele bases. Nearby is Silla Millennium Storage, the Yeongnam regional storage facility opened in 2019. It holds around 600,000 artifacts excavated in the Yeongnam region, with approximately 3,000 available to view in its display storage area. Exhibition interpretation programs are also offered in the Silla History, Silla Art, and Wolji galleries, so check the schedule before visiting.

260: Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in December 2000, the Gyeongju Historic Areas preserve the history and culture of Gyeongju, the ancient capital of Silla (57–935). The sites are divided into five areas according to their characteristics: the Namsan Area, a treasury of Buddhist art; the Wolseong Area, the palace site of a thousand-year dynasty; the Daereungwon Area, home to ancient tombs including those of Silla kings; the Hwangnyongsa Area, representing the essence of Silla Buddhism; and the Sanseong Area, central to the royal capital's defenses. The World Heritage property includes 52 designated cultural heritage sites. The Namsan Area includes the Stone Seated Buddha in Mireukgok Valley on Namsan Mountain, Gyeongju; the Three-Story Stone Pagoda in Yongjangsagok Valley on Namsan Mountain; the Stone Well at Namgansa Temple Site; and the Rock-Carved Seated Buddha in Bulgok Valley on Namsan Mountain. The Wolseong Area includes Gyerim Forest, Wolseong Palace Site, Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond, and Cheomseongdae Observatory. The Daereungwon Area includes the Tomb of King Michu, the Five Royal Tombs, and the Ancient Tombs in Nodong-ri. The Hwangnyongsa Area includes Hwangnyongsa Temple Site and the Stone Brick Pagoda of Bunhwangsa Temple, while the Sanseong Area includes Myeonghwal Fortress.
269: Gyeongju's Jjoksaem District refers to the Hwango-ri ancient tomb area east of Daereungwon, encompassing Hwango-dong, Hwangnam-dong, and Inwang-dong. A collective burial ground for Silla royalty and nobility from the 4th to 6th centuries, it covers approximately 384,000 m² and is a leading Korean excavation site for artifacts associated with Silla's royal and noble families. As housing construction from the 1960s onward seriously damaged the tomb remains, the Cultural Heritage Administration and Gyeongju City purchased private houses and land in the area and began excavations in 2007. Gyeongju City built the two-story Jjoksaem Excavation Museum, with a total floor area of about 1,900 m². It includes artifact storage and an interior visitor walkway overlooking the excavation area. The entire second floor is finished in glass, providing a panoramic view of the Jjoksaem excavation site. Visitors can directly observe the excavation of this tomb district, Korea's largest collective burial ground for royalty and nobility, and see exhibits with accounts and photographs of the excavation process and the tombs uncovered.
278: Jeonchon Dragon Caves in Gampo, Gyeongju, are natural sculptures created by waves and time. These sea caves lie along the coast near Jeonchon Port. There are two, Saryonggul and Danyonggul, and, as their names suggest, both have dragon legends. Four dragons guarding the four cardinal directions are said to have lived in Saryonggul, while a single dragon protecting Gampo village lived in Danyonggul. With passages that seem fit for dragons to come and go, the caves are stops on sections 1 and 8 of Gampo Kkakjigil, Gampo-eup's storytelling walking trail. They can also be seen along section 11 of the Haep arang Trail on the east coast. Until recently, the area was closed to civilians as a military operations zone. As the Haep arang Trail began to take shape, a wooden coastal walkway was installed, making Saryonggul relatively easy to reach.
286: 'Silla in Brilliant Light' is a timeless media art exhibition at Cheonma Palace in Gyeongju Expo Grand Park. Its cutting-edge displays let visitors interact directly with the works through media art imagery, vividly conveying the value of Gyeongju's UNESCO World Heritage history and cultural heritage. Representative sites such as Cheomseongdae, Seokguram, Bulguksa, and Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond are depicted through colorful, dreamlike media art. The works respond to visitors' movements, making this an interactive exhibition the whole family can enjoy, beyond simply viewing the art.
294: EX HORROR Season 6: Silla X Zombies
295: EX HORROR Season 6: Silla X Zombies is a midsummer-night walking horror experience held in Hwarang Forest at Gyeongju Expo Grand Park. Attracting more than 15,000 visitors each year, EX HORROR combines a variety of horror experiences along the forest's 2 km walking trail. Visitors of all ages can participate, but admission is restricted for older or physically vulnerable people and those with medical conditions because of potential health issues. Preschool children must enter with an adult guardian.
